repair_cafe_item_visit_outcome.description: You bring a broken toaster or a torn coat to a repair cafe, a volunteer takes it on, and your visit ends one of three ways. About six in ten visits end with the item working again, about one in seven with advice to take home, and about one in four with a repair that failed. What tells these apart most is how long the repair ran: items that were repaired typically sit around p36 of repair_minutes, those that ended in advice around p65 and failed ones around p86. The fault called at the intake desk comes next: most items with a minor fault get repaired, while most with a major fault fail. Older items fail more often too, with failed repairs around p84 of item_age_years against p42 for items that were repaired. total_minutes follows the time spent, while wait_minutes and item_type carry little. Something the records do not capture also matters.

columns.item_age_years: How old the item is, in whole years, as the visitor reports it.
columns.item_type: The broad kind of item: a small appliance such as a kettle, electronics such as a radio, a textile such as a coat, or furniture.
columns.fault_severity: How bad the fault looks to the volunteer at the intake desk, before anyone opens the item.
columns.wait_minutes: How long the visitor waited before a volunteer could start. It shares a cause with how the visit ends.
columns.repair_minutes: How long a volunteer worked on the item; some records leave it blank.
columns.total_minutes: The wait and the repair added together, worked out from those two columns.
columns.outcome: How the visit ended: repaired means the item works again, advice_given means the visitor left with advice on fixing it at home, and repair_failed means the attempt did not work.
